books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: Thirteenth Amendment to the Constitution (ratified December 6, 1865)

stimulus.text:
“Section 1. Neither slavery nor involuntary servitude, except as a punishment for crime whereof the party shall have been duly convicted, shall exist within the United States, or any place subject to their jurisdiction. Section 2. Congress shall have power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation.”

—Thirteenth Amendment, ratified December 6, 1865
stimulus.source_note: Thirteenth Amendment, ratified December 6, 1865. Public domain. Wording verified against the Constitution Annotated (Congress.gov).

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The exception in Section 1, “except as a punishment for crime,” meant that

options.text: slavery could continue on any plantation.
options.misconception: Background: the amendment bans slavery as an institution; the exception is narrow, not a plantation loophole.

options.text: the amendment did not apply in the South.
options.misconception: Background: the amendment applied to the whole country, South included.

options.text: Congress could not enforce the amendment.
options.misconception: Background: Section 2 gives Congress the power to enforce the amendment.

options.text: forced labor remained legal as a criminal punishment.

rationales.A: Background: the amendment bans slavery as an institution; the exception is narrow, not a plantation loophole.
rationales.B: Background: the amendment applied to the whole country, South included.
rationales.C: Background: Section 2 gives Congress the power to enforce the amendment.
rationales.D: The exception is written into the ban itself: slavery and involuntary servitude are gone, except when a person has been duly convicted of a crime. That narrow opening later let states lease convicted laborers, a practice the amendment itself allowed.
rationales.general:
1. Read the ban straight through: no slavery, except as punishment for a crime after a conviction.
2. The exception is small, but it is written into the Constitution.
3. Background: Southern states later used it to lease prisoners as laborers.
4. So the amendment ended slavery and left one narrow door open.
Remember: an exception inside a ban is part of the ban, not a footnote to it.
